reviewer: Grok (independent read-only check of the spawn-attribute analysis; did not author it)
subject: reports/sprint-010/shared-shell-first-app-sigkill-spawnattr-analysis-001.json
verdict: The mechanism is not refuted. F1 through F9 stand, with the precisions below. F10 is a real caveat and its 'never killed' sentence is too strong for one file-descriptor case. The uninitialized bytes and the claim that this path ran for pid 14 remain unestablished. D4 is worth one diagnostic boot of a new candidate. This check does not authorize that boot.

evidence.libsystem_extracted: debugfs 1.47.4 -n dumped /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib from candidate-003 ramdisk.img. 4202078 bytes, sha256 8ff49e0c2a5f1c6532101c7ed662632444cc97ae9669479090e7968deddd12ff. llvm-objdump 22.1.8 of _posix_spawnattr_init at 0xa8988. The image hash was rechecked as dd482a77.
evidence.kernel: candidate-003 kernel.macho 38965160 bytes sha256 02fe2d4106ca3091b95a3e9235e3f9a7226c0f030eb24fb609f6817506c0f883. Version string at file offset 1289544. File-descriptor string at 1295334, mach-ports string at 1294921, kqworkloops string at 1295113, token-ident string at 1295009.

findings.F1_libsystem_binary: CONFIRMED. malloc immediate is 0xf8. The only stores are the claimed offsets 0x00, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x0c, 0x10, 0x18, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x40, 0x42, 0x44, 0x48, 0x4c, 0x50, 0x58, 0x5c, 0x60, 0x68, 0x6a, 0x6c, 0x70, 0x78, 0x80, 0xc0, 0xc8, 0xd0, 0xd8, 0xe0, 0xe8. Byte 0x69 and 0x84-0xbf are never written. Also unwritten: pad byte 0x6b, pads 0x9c-0x9f and 0xa9 inside the copied prefix, and 0xf0-0xf7 (psa_conclave_id), which is past offsetof(psa_ports). The exported malloc calls _malloc_zone_malloc with MZ_POSIX (0x1), which only sets errno on failure, then zone->malloc. That wrapper does not bzero.
findings.F2_libsystem_source: CONFIRMED. PureDarwin posix_spawnattr_init assigns through psa_options and does not assign psa_4k or any limit, crash, launch, sec, or conclave field. posix_spawn sets ad.attr_size to sizeof(struct _posix_spawnattr) when attrp is set (posix_spawn.c 2682). The dylib exports no setter for those fields. Its spawnattr exports stop at flags, pgroup, sigdefault, sigmask, and binpref.
findings.F3_pinned_reference: CONFIRMED. xnu __posix_spawnattr_init zeroes psa_4k, psa_tecs, the port, filedesc, and kqworkloop limits, conclave memory, crash behavior and deadline, launch type, dataless policy, sec flags, crash count, throttle, and psa_conclave_id.
findings.F4_layout: CONFIRMED. The binary stores match the LP64 header: psa_4k at 0x69, psa_options at 0x80, limits and the other new scalars at 0x84-0xbc, psa_ports at 0xc0, and the following pointers through psa_subsystem_root_path at 0xe8. sizeof 248 matches the malloc.
findings.F5_kernel_copy_and_apply: CONFIRMED. kern_exec.c 4358 sets px_sa_offset to offsetof(psa_ports). Line 4452 copyin of that many bytes runs when attr_size is nonzero. Lines 5364-5378, inside CONFIG_PROC_RESOURCE_LIMITS, call task_set_port_space_limits, proc_set_filedesc_limits, and proc_set_kqworkloop_limits when the corresponding soft or hard value is greater than 0. File descriptors reset soft to 0 when soft >= hard and hard > 0 (kern_proc.c 5487-5491). Ports do the same (ipc_space.c 503-505). proc_set_kqworkloop_limits stores both values with no such reset.
findings.F6_kernel_build: CONFIRMED. The booted kernel identifies itself as xnu-12377.121.6~1/DEBUG_ARM64_T8103. config/MASTER.arm64 puts config_proc_resource_limits in KERNEL_DEBUG, and DEBUG includes KERNEL_DEBUG. The file-descriptor os_log and 'Unable to create task token ident object' are compiled inside CONFIG_PROC_RESOURCE_LIMITS, so their presence in this image shows the flag is on. The mach-ports 'caught allocating' string is outside that ifdef and does not, by itself, prove the flag.
findings.F7_kill_path: CONFIRMED, with one precision on the last send right. A hard-limit AST on the current thread reaches ast.c 387-392, which runs task_port_space_ast and then proc_filedesc_ast. The hard-limit arms in task.c allocate one send right with task_allocate_fatal_port (IPC_KOBJECT_ALLOC_MAKE_SEND, IKOT_TASK_FATAL). IKOT_TASK_FATAL registers task_fatal_port_no_senders, and ipc_kobject_register_startup sets pol_notif_no_senders because that operation is set. After send_resource_violation_with_fatal_port, the caller ipc_port_release_send goes through ipc_port_release_send_and_unlock, which calls ipc_notify_no_senders_emit inline. For an active kobject that calls ipc_notify_no_senders_kobject and then task_fatal_port_no_senders on the same thread. That calls task_identity_token_try_sigkill, which psignal(SIGKILL)s with a null reason (bsd_kern.c 120-139). psignal_internal then build_signal_reason(SIGKILL, NULL), which names current_proc() and copies the whole p_name (kern_sig.c 2447-2452 and 1978-2022). The fatal port argument is mach_port_copy_send_t. A message that stays queued holds a second send right, so no-senders would later run on whoever destroys that right, and the kcdata sender would be that process. host_get_special_port returns KERN_SUCCESS for an empty slot. The send then fails, the copied right dies with the message, and the caller's release is the last send right, still on this thread. Candidate-004's ramdisk contains the bytes HostSpecialPort only as launchd's key string (three hits) and contains no ResourceNotify bytes. This image has no configured resource-notify receiver, so the inline victim-thread drop is the path the source takes. If task_allocate_fatal_port fails, task_self_sigkill uses OS_REASON_RESOURCES, which is a different record. A hard limit of 0 takes the soft arm and allocates no fatal port.
findings.F8_record_match: CONFIRMED as a shape match only. A victim-thread psignal(SIGKILL) with a null reason produces OS_REASON_SIGNAL code 9 whose sender is current_proc(), including the full p_name copy seen in attempts 002 and 003. That match does not show that this path ran.
findings.F9_console_absence_is_not_evidence: CONFIRMED. os_log goes through _os_log_internal with driverKit false, then _os_log_to_msgbuf_internal, then vprintf_log_locked. subr_prf.c 432-435 sets TOLOGLOCKED and adds TOCONS only when the driverkit argument is true. These resource-limit lines are not DriverKit logs. Their absence from the serial console neither confirms nor refutes the path. log_dmesg copies the newest bytes when the caller buffer is smaller than the log (subr_log.c 781-787).
findings.F10_notify_misdirection_caveat: CONFIRMED as a caveat, and the sentence 'the child is never killed' is too strong. fd_check_limit_exceeded and kqworkloop_check_limit_exceeded call act_set_astproc_resource(current_thread()). proc_set_filedesc_limits and proc_set_kqworkloop_limits call those checks during posix_spawn, while current_thread is the parent, and they set the notified flag on the child immediately. The if/else prefers the soft limit. If the count already exceeds both, only the soft flag is set. A later allocation on the child's own thread can still take the hard branch and kill the child. Port limits are different: ipc_space_set_table_size_limits does not check the current table. The port check runs later in ipc_entries_hold, on the thread that grows the table. A hard limit that is above the count at exec and is crossed later on the child's thread remains a real way to get a victim-sender SIGKILL. It is not the only way for file descriptors.

not_established: the byte values in 0x84-0xbf at the first spawn
that the resource-limit path ran for pid 14
which limit, if any, was crossed
why a later spawn received harmless values
that the desktop heap reused a 256-byte slot rather than a fresh zeroed page
d4: Still a useful test of this candidate, and worth one bounded boot. The expected outcome is that the first app dies again. A kept line that contains 'caught allocating too many' and names chonk-terminal-d[PID] would confirm the path and the limit. A read as euid 0 with matched=0 counts against the mechanism. query_failed or unsupported leaves it untested. D4 does not change the launch and does not fix the SIGKILL.
not_claimed: that the SIGKILL cause is established
scope: Read-only. debugfs -n, llvm-objdump, llvm-nm, and the pinned XNU and libSystem sources named above. No mount, no source edit, no cargo, no SSH, and no hardware.
